content.title: About
content.content: Pinto beans are a variety of dry legume popular in Mexican and South American cuisines. White rice is a polished grain that has had its husk and bran removed. Together they form a nutritious, filling dish often used as a side or a base for stews.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “pinto” comes from the Spanish word for “spotted,” referring to the bean’s mottled appearance.
Rice is one of the world’s most consumed foods; more than half of the global population eats rice regularly.
Combining beans and rice provides a complete set of essential amino acids, making the meal a complete protein source.
In traditional Mexican cuisine, pinto beans are commonly served with rice, tomatoes, onions, and spices in a dish called “arroz con frijoles.”
Pinto beans are rich in antioxidants, especially polyphenols, which give them their characteristic color.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Pinto beans contain about 21 g of protein per 100 g dry weight, and rice complements their amino‑acid profile.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber in beans supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Provides complex carbohydrates
items.content: White rice offers a quick energy source, while the beans slow the release of carbs for steadier blood sugar.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Both foods are good sources of thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals and trace elements
items.content: Pinto beans supply iron, magnesium and potassium; rice adds phosphorus and modest amounts of zinc.

items.title: Phytic acid
items.content: Beans contain phytates that can reduce mineral absorption; soaking and sprouting lower their levels.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: High glycemic index of rice
items.content: White rice has a high GI, which can raise blood sugar quickly; pairing it with fiber and protein mitigates the effect.

items.title: Food poisoning from undercooking
items.content: Undercooked beans may contain toxic lectins; they should be boiled for at least 10 minutes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook pinto beans and white rice separately until tender, then combine and season with salt, pepper, garlic, onion, or your favorite spices. Use them as a side dish, base for chili, salads, casseroles, or a simple rice‑and‑bean bowl.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry beans in an airtight container in a cool, dry place for up to 1 year. Cooked beans and rice keep in the refrigerator in a sealed container for 4‑5 days, or freeze in portions for longer storage.
